findings.title: apiBase fallback to http://localhost:8080 with no production guard (deferred)
findings.description: Round 1 finding (major) re-classified as deferred per commit message and decisions.md context. nuxt.config.ts still falls back to http://localhost:8080 if NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE is unset. Re-noting here so the deferral remains visible. No new code change in commit 477048b touched this surface.
findings.impact: Misconfigured production deploy could ship a bundle pointing at localhost:8080 with credentials:'include'.
findings.recommendation: Track in backlog; add an env-var guard in nuxt.config.ts before the next deploy that builds the frontend bundle (throw if NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE is missing in production).

findings.title: fetchUser only clears userState on 401 (deferred)
findings.description: Round 1 finding (major) deferred. fetchUser() in stores/auth.ts still leaves userState populated when a non-401 error occurs (e.g., 403, 5xx, network), which can produce stale 'authenticated' UI on a server-side terminated session. Tests added in this commit (fetchUser_500Response_propagatesErrorAndKeepsUser) explicitly codify the deferred behavior, so the gap is documented.
findings.impact: User UI may display authenticated state after backend session has been invalidated by an error other than 401.
findings.recommendation: Track in backlog; consider fail-closed semantics (clear user on any /api/auth/me failure) in a follow-up.

findings.title: useState SSR cross-request leak risk in non-default Nuxt deployments (deferred)
findings.description: Round 1 finding (major) deferred. Middleware now calls fetchUser() whenever authStore.user === null (including on /auth/** routes — improvement from round 1), but still short-circuits when user is non-null. In default Nuxt runtime useState is per-request; in non-standard deployments this is still a residual risk. Acknowledged by team and acceptable for current default deployment topology.
findings.impact: Cross-request authentication bleed only in non-default Nuxt server configurations.
findings.recommendation: Track in backlog; add a regression test covering two SSR renders with different cookies before introducing custom server adapters.

findings.title: No CSP / X-Frame-Options / Referrer-Policy at the Nuxt level (deferred)
findings.description: Round 1 minor finding deferred. nuxt.config.ts still configures no nitro routeRules with security headers and no nuxt-security module. Defense-in-depth gap remains; not blocking.
findings.impact: Missing layered defense against future XSS / clickjacking regressions; relies entirely on reverse proxy / hosting.
findings.recommendation: Track in backlog; add nitro routeRules with CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin in a follow-up.

findings.title: happy-dom@16.8.1 has known advisories (deferred)
findings.description: Round 1 minor finding deferred. happy-dom is still pinned at ^16.5.3 (resolves to 16.8.1) in package.json. devDependency only, used by vitest — no production runtime impact. Supply-chain risk for CI if untrusted PR test fixtures are ever introduced.
findings.impact: CI compromise vector for runs with untrusted PR fixtures; no production runtime impact.
findings.recommendation: Track in backlog; bump to happy-dom@^17.4.5 and add `pnpm audit` step to CI in a follow-up.

round_1_critical_csrf.evidence: useApi() now installs an onRequest interceptor that (a) skips SAFE methods (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS), (b) reads the XSRF-TOKEN cookie via document.cookie regex with decodeURIComponent (handles base64 padding correctly), (c) clones existing headers via new Headers() and sets X-XSRF-TOKEN, (d) is SSR-safe via the import.meta.client + typeof document guard so it no-ops cleanly on server-side $fetch (no token needed because no state-changing requests are made during SSR bootstrap). Implementation matches tech-spec Decision 12 (CookieCsrfTokenRepository.withHttpOnlyFalse + X-XSRF-TOKEN header) and the round 1 fix recommendation. Logout (POST /api/auth/logout) and all future state-changing requests will now include the CSRF token.
implementation_quality_notes: Header type cast `as HeadersInit | undefined` is correct for ofetch's options.headers type.
Regex `(?:^|;\s*)XSRF-TOKEN=([^;]+)` correctly anchors to cookie-name boundary (no partial-match false positives on cookies whose name ends in XSRF-TOKEN).
decodeURIComponent on the token value matches Spring Security CookieCsrfTokenRepository behavior (token is URL-encoded in the cookie).
SAFE_METHODS set follows RFC 7231 / OWASP guidance.
No token leak via console.log or telemetry.

new_changes_reviewed.frontend/middleware/auth.global.ts: Now calls fetchUser() whenever user is null (including on /auth/** routes) — strictly better than round 1 (closes the SSR-state-pollution short-circuit on /auth/**). try/catch swallows non-401 errors so navigation always completes; combined with store's '401-only clears state' behavior this means a 5xx during navigation leaves user as null (correct). No new security regression.
new_changes_reviewed.frontend/layouts/default.vue: Logout handler wraps authStore.logout() in try/catch so navigateTo('/auth/login') always runs; store's finally clause guarantees local userState is cleared before the throw. Net effect: even if backend logout fails (e.g., CSRF mismatch, network drop), the user is redirected to login and local state is cleared. This is acceptable for a UX fail-closed behavior; no security regression introduced.
new_changes_reviewed.frontend/tests/stores/auth.spec.ts: New tests (fetchUser_500Response_propagatesErrorAndKeepsUser, logout_apiError_stillClearsUser) codify the deferred 401-only-clear behavior. fetchUser_401Response_setsUserNull is now non-tautological (pre-arms ACTIVE_USER). No new security concern.
new_changes_reviewed.frontend/tests/middleware/auth.global.sp: Per the commit stat, adds backend-error and valid-session-on-/auth/login regression tests. These exercise the new behavior of always calling fetchUser when user is null. No new security concern.
new_changes_reviewed.frontend/package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml: Drops the explicit `vue` dep (now transitive via nuxt) — eliminates the dup-Vue-copies risk. No new security concern.
